content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to PLC programming and ladder logic. My background is in electrical engineering, mostly building control panels with relays and timers for ovens and compressors. I understand the operational needs and am able to implement them using traditional methods, but now I'm starting to explore PLCs. I selected the [product_name] since it seemed to suit my requirements. I've watched many tutorials online and grasp the basics of ladder programming. Any advice, helpful hints, or recommendations to deepen my understanding would be welcome. Thank you.
Welcome to the forum. Are you just introducing yourself, or do you have specific technical questions you'd like to discuss?

Hi, I currently live in Devon and work for a steel company, handling machine installations and process improvements. I've spent 30 years in electrical work, focusing on industrial and commercial environments. I've recently started working with PLCs, although my experience has mostly been with control systems built from relays and timers. I'm eager to learn. My first PLC project is modernizing a powder coating oven; the gas burner works fine, but the control setup is outdated. I know how I'd like it to operate and could implement it with relays and timers, but I want to switch to PLC control. I've written a basic ladder program for timed on/off sequences. I'd appreciate any help or guidance, specifically on how to increase the diagram page length in the programming software, as I've run out of space.

In the diagram editor's menu bar, there's a small icon showing a four-square diagram labeled 1, 2, 3, 4. Hovering over it reveals it as the 'page layout' tool. Clicking this lets you configure the number of diagram pages vertically and horizontally.
Thanks for the info. If you're interested, could you take a look at my program and provide some input or feedback?
We can't review your program unless you share it. Please attach it as a zip file in your next post.

I've attached the beginning of my program. I'm very new to programming, still learning the basics. What I want to achieve includes: 1) Turn on fans for 1 minute; 2) After that timer, start the ignition sequence (a closed 24V signal confirms ignition); 3) The ignition signal then initiates stage 3 heating, timed for 1 minute. So far, that's working. Now, after stage 3 heating, I'd like the PLC to regulate the burner: raise oven temperature to 180°C, then switch the burner off until it drops by 5°C, then back on, repeating as necessary. Once the oven reaches 150°C, it should only burn for 12 minutes, after which the burner shuts off by removing the signal to Q2. When the oven cools to 60°C, the fans should shut down. This process is currently handled manually with a sounder to alert the operator to begin shutdown. Any help or advice to automate this would be much appreciated. Thanks.

It's a good idea to first outline all the inputs and outputs needed, along with their functions and hardware list. For example: Digital inputs—like I1: Stop button (NC), I2: Start button (NO), I3: Stage 3 trigger (NC), I4: [unspecified], etc. Digital outputs—such as Q1: Fans on, Q2: Gas on, Q3: Burner on, Q4: [unspecified], etc. Are analog inputs required? If so, how many sensors? Will you need analog expansion modules?

Thank you for the tip. I'll be back at work Monday and will try to list all the relevant hardware and functions. My goal is to fully understand PLC programming; traditional relays and timers make sense to me, but I know PLCs are the way forward. I can handle wiring diagrams, but I want to learn PLC logic and hope it's not too late to start.

It's definitely not too late. Even though the [product_name] isn't a traditional PLC—it's marketed more as a programmable logic module—it now offers much more functionality than earlier models. Before programming, however, it's best to plan and document the concept, including all hardware requirements.

Good morning. The components I plan to use are: [product_name] power module, logic module, [product_name] expansion module, [product_name] analog module, and [product_name] operator device. I have an idea of how I want the system to function and which inputs/outputs to use, but I'm still trying to determine the best approach. Briefly: Input 1 is for Emergency OFF; Input 2 is the Start button (which initiates a timer, fan start, etc.); Input 3 handles the ignition sequence; Input 4 connects to a contact that closes on successful ignition, triggering a timer and opening the stage 3 valve. This allows the oven to heat to 150°C, at which point a timer runs for 12 minutes and then ends the heating sequence by controlling Input 3. Once temperature falls below 60°C, the fans will shut down. On the panel, I'll have an emergency stop, a start button, and a stop button to end the ignition sequence. I might add an alarm for the end of the 12-minute cycle, and possibly an HMI display if needed. Hopefully this clarifies things. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is shifting from relay-based control panel designs to PLC-based automation using [company_name] programmable modules. Early challenges included adjusting diagram page sizes in the programming environment, highlighting the need for beginner-friendly software tools. Throughout the discussion, there was a focus on understanding PLC logic, structured planning before programming, and identifying suitable hardware components for the project.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates beginner-friendly software navigation, straightforward ladder diagram expansion, and supportive resources or community guidance to help master PLC logic and programming.
